12 October 2026 · Pocket Flight private tester · codex/private-wind-tunnel

Detailed, animated aircraft mechanisms

All four aircraft now have a mechanical showcase in the private tester. Native articulated parts retain their authoring hierarchy, while supplemental instanced hardware follows their attachment points. Analytical mode uses the existing neutral model and measured wing geometry.

Open the private tester · Chamber rebuild · Aerodynamic scope

What moves

  • Ailerons, flaps, elevators, rudders and available canards, with linked hydraulic barrels, polished pistons, hinge fittings and flexible hoses.
  • Fixed-gear suspension and steering on Finch; retractable gear and sequenced bay doors on the jets. Aurelia uses its exported Blender gear curves; Stormbird uses its CAD mechanism datums, including braces, torque links, steering and canopy rams.
  • Suspension pressure travel, folding scissor links, rotating wheels, brake rotors, stationary calipers and flexible brake hoses.
  • Propeller/compressor/fan rotation at a deliberately slow inspection speed. Peregrine and Stormbird each gain 32 articulated nozzle petals whose aperture responds to the programme’s power command.
  • Supplemental control sticks, throttle levers and rudder pedals on the jets. Peregrine’s canopy and Stormbird’s canopy open during their access sequence; Aurelia retains its fixed flight deck. Finch’s rebuilt cockpit has native dual sticks, pedals and a complete rear-hinged canopy with authored support mounts.

Finch cockpit rebuilt

Finch’s complete cabin has been replaced with a lower instrument panel, contoured bucket seats, compact avionics and a complete rear-hinged canopy. Its native hinge and support mounts now drive the mechanism; the previous guessed window actuators are gone. See the cockpit rebuild and inspection report.

Actual motion recording

9.97-second MP4, 828 × 736, 299 frames. Captured from the running Three.js canvas. The recorded Stormbird gear command moves from 0.021 extension to 1.0 while the native braces, rams and pressure mechanism follow.

Use the showcase

Choose an aircraft and press Run mechanical showcase. Select All systems, Gear & suspension, Flight controls, Propulsion, or Cockpit & access. The 36-second cycle slider follows playback; dragging it pauses at a precise pose. Pause/resume holds every mechanism. Gear and cockpit close-ups automatically reveal the shell; the checkbox also controls that view manually. Return to aerodynamics restores the neutral representation and overlays.

1440 × 1000, Chromium with Metal, DPR 1, about 1.3 seconds of active rendering per aircraft. The samples use the shell states shown in the table. This is a local short benchmark, not a sustained or cross-device result.

Supplemental rams, hoses, collars, brake hardware and cockpit fittings share five instanced pools. Fighter nozzle petals add one pool. Native static meshes are batched within each moving assembly. The mechanical hierarchy is built lazily; inactive GPU buffers are released on mode changes, and paused views stop drawing. Hidden aerodynamic overlays are not animated during the showcase. The scrubber updates independently of the main React interface.

Verification

113 repository tests pass with 47,257 assertions after the cockpit rebuild. The tester and game production builds pass. Thirty-five fleet mechanism browser checks and seven dedicated cockpit checks pass with zero browser/shader errors. The saved Finch Blender file was independently reopened, and the shared GLB passed a game free-flight smoke check.

This is a concept mechanical inspection programme. Rotation is slowed for visibility. The supplemental geometry is generated at runtime in the private tester; Finch’s shared GLB includes the rebuilt cockpit; the other source aircraft and flight behavior remain intact. Force readouts retain the neutral main-wing reference and do not calculate aerodynamic changes from the posed controls, gear or canopy.
